cover.creator: <Creator>
cover.statistics_note: WF01 Onboarding, WF02 Auto-reply, WF03 Incident Recovery, WF04 Lead Pipeline, WF05 Content Pipeline

environment:
1. Frontend: React + Vite (localhost:15876)
2. API Backend: .NET 8 (localhost:15874)
3. AgentService gRPC (localhost:15875)
4. Gateway: .NET 10 Ocelot (localhost:15873)
5. SQL Server 2022 (Docker :1433)
6. Redis 7 (Docker :6379)
7. Qdrant (Docker :6333)
8. MinIO (Docker :9001)
9. RabbitMQ (Docker :15672)

workflows.name: Tenant onboarding and initial configuration
workflows.requirement: Create a new tenant, configure an LLM provider, connect a channel, grant roles and verify the first sign-in and permission fence
workflows.precondition: The full stack is running (all services up); an admin seed account exists

cases.description: Create a new tenant from the admin panel
cases.procedure:
1. Sign in as system admin.
2. Open system settings and create a new tenant with a unique name.
cases.expected: The tenant is created and visible in the tenant list with status active.
cases.precondition: System admin account is seeded

cases.description: Create the first admin user for the new tenant
cases.procedure:
1. Open the new tenant.
2. Create an admin user account with a temporary password.
cases.expected: The user is created; a welcome email is sent; the user can sign in.
cases.precondition: The tenant was created in TC-ST-ONB-001

cases.description: Sign in as the new tenant admin and change the temporary password
cases.procedure:
1. Sign in with the temporary password.
2. Follow the password-change prompt.
3. Sign in again with the new password.
cases.expected: Password change succeeds; the temporary password is no longer accepted; the dashboard loads.
cases.precondition: TC-ST-ONB-002 has been completed

cases.description: Navigation menu reflects the granted role permissions
cases.procedure:
1. Create a user with a restricted role (conversations:read only).
2. Sign in as that user.
cases.expected: Only the Inbox section is visible; /leads, /content, /kb, /agents are inaccessible.
cases.precondition: A restricted role has been created and granted

cases.description: Configure an LLM provider with a valid API key
cases.procedure:
1. Open LLM Providers (/llm-providers).
2. Add a provider (e.g. OpenAI) with a valid API key.
3. Save and run the connection test.
cases.expected: Provider is saved; connection test returns success; status shows active.
cases.precondition: A valid API key is available in the test environment

cases.description: Reject an LLM provider URL that points to a private host without a grant
cases.procedure:
1. Attempt to save an LLM provider with baseUrl = http://192.168.1.10:8080.
2. Submit without enabling private host access.
cases.expected: Save is rejected with an SSRF-guard error; no provider row is persisted.
cases.precondition: allowPrivateHosts is false (default)

cases.description: Connect a Facebook channel and verify the first message sync
cases.procedure:
1. Open system channels (/system/channels).
2. Connect a Facebook page with a valid token.
3. Wait for the initial sync.
cases.expected: Channel shows as connected; existing conversations appear in /conversations within a few minutes.
cases.precondition: A Facebook test page and valid token are available
cases.note: Round 1: the channel reported connected but no inbox row was created, so the first sync produced no conversation. Fixed and retested in round 2.

cases.description: Updating a tenant name is audited
cases.procedure:
1. PUT /api/tenants/{id} with a new name.
2. GET /api/audit?entity=tenant.
cases.expected: Name is updated; an audit row records the change with actor and timestamp.
cases.precondition: Tenant admin is signed in

cases.description: Deactivating a tenant blocks its users from signing in
cases.procedure:
1. Deactivate tenant B.
2. Attempt to sign in as a tenant B user.
cases.expected: Sign-in is rejected with HTTP 403; audit row is present.
cases.precondition: Tenant B exists with an active user

workflows.name: End-to-end auto-reply, handover and lead creation
workflows.requirement: Receive an inbound message, answer it automatically using the knowledge base, pause when a sales agent intervenes, resume after the pause window, and create a scored lead from the conversation
workflows.precondition: A channel is connected; a knowledge base is deployed; auto-reply is enabled on the test conversation

cases.description: Receive an inbound message and get an automatic reply
cases.procedure:
1. Send a message from the test channel that matches a KB topic.
2. Wait up to 30 seconds.
cases.expected: An automatic outbound reply is sent; the reply text reflects the KB content.
cases.precondition: Auto-reply is enabled; KB is deployed and indexed

cases.description: Decline to answer when no KB content covers the question
cases.procedure:
1. Send a message on a topic completely outside the KB.
2. Wait up to 30 seconds.
cases.expected: The auto-reply sends a safe fallback message and optionally escalates to a human agent.
cases.precondition: Auto-reply is enabled; the question is outside all KB modules

cases.description: Deduplicate a message delivered by both webhook and polling
cases.procedure:
1. Enable both ingestion paths.
2. Send a single message from the channel.
cases.expected: Exactly one auto-reply is sent; exactly one message record is stored.
cases.precondition: Both ingestion paths are active

cases.description: A manual reply by a sales agent pauses auto-reply
cases.procedure:
1. Sign in as a sales agent.
2. Send a manual reply on the conversation.
3. Send a new inbound message from the channel.
cases.expected: Auto-reply stays silent for the configured pause window (default 5 minutes).
cases.precondition: Auto-reply is enabled on the conversation

cases.description: Auto-reply resumes after the pause window without manual action
cases.procedure:
1. Trigger a pause by sending a manual reply.
2. Advance time past the pause window (or wait).
3. Send a new inbound message.
cases.expected: The sweep job re-enables auto-reply; the new message gets an automatic response.
cases.precondition: A pause was triggered; the TryResumeAiAutoReply sweep job is running
cases.note: Round 1: the sweep resumed new conversations but left the one that was already waiting before the pause. Fixed and retested in round 2.

cases.description: Manually disabling auto-reply prevents automatic resumption
cases.procedure:
1. Toggle auto-reply OFF via the conversation UI.
2. Advance time past the default pause window.
3. Send a new inbound message.
cases.expected: Auto-reply remains disabled (resume_at is null); no automatic response is sent.
cases.precondition: Auto-reply was explicitly toggled off

cases.description: Create a lead from a conversation and verify the initial score
cases.procedure:
1. Open a conversation that has contact details.
2. Create a lead from the conversation panel.
3. Inspect the lead score on /leads.
cases.expected: Lead is created; score is calculated based on the lead scoring rules; pipeline stage reflects the score (cold / warm / hot).
cases.precondition: The conversation has an identifiable contact; lead scoring rules are seeded

cases.description: Lead score increases when a purchase-intent event is recorded
cases.procedure:
1. Open the lead created in TC-ST-ARP-007.
2. Record a purchase_intent activity.
3. Refresh the lead card.
cases.expected: The lead score increases by the purchase_intent delta (default +20); pipeline stage may advance.
cases.precondition: TC-ST-ARP-007 completed; lead is in cold or warm stage

cases.description: Reactivate a lost lead when new inbound activity arrives
cases.procedure:
1. Mark a lead as lost.
2. Send a new inbound message from the same contact.
cases.expected: The lead is reactivated; LastActivityAt is updated; the lost status is cleared.
cases.precondition: A lost lead exists for the contact

cases.description: Feedback flag on an auto-reply is recorded
cases.procedure: 1. Mark an auto-reply as not helpful via POST /api/inbox/messages/{id}/feedback.
cases.expected: Feedback is stored and visible in the conversation audit.
cases.precondition: An auto-reply message exists

cases.description: Escalated conversation appears in the escalation queue
cases.procedure:
1. POST /api/inbox/conversations/{id}/escalate.
2. GET /api/inbox/escalated.
cases.expected: Conversation is listed as escalated; auto-reply is disabled.
cases.precondition: Conversation is open

workflows.name: Recovery from job failures, queue outages and KB deploy errors
workflows.requirement: Failed background jobs are retried and logged; message queue outages do not lose messages; a KB deploy failure leaves the previous version active and is surfaced in the error log
workflows.precondition: Hangfire job scheduler and RabbitMQ are running; the system error log tab is accessible

cases.description: A Hangfire job that fails is retried the configured number of times
cases.procedure:
1. Inject a transient failure into a job handler.
2. Observe the Hangfire dashboard or job logs.
cases.expected: The job is retried up to the configured retry count, then marked as failed with the error recorded.
cases.precondition: Retry count is configured; Hangfire dashboard is accessible

cases.description: A failed job appears in the system error log
cases.procedure:
1. Let a job fail permanently (exhaust retries).
2. Open the error log tab (/logs).
cases.expected: The failure entry is listed with its exception type, message and timestamp.
cases.precondition: TC-ST-REC-001 has been completed

cases.description: A Hangfire job runs in an isolated DI scope with the correct tenant context
cases.procedure:
1. Trigger a scheduled job for a specific tenant.
2. Verify the job reads and writes data only for that tenant.
cases.expected: No cross-tenant data contamination; ITenantOwned query filters are applied.
cases.precondition: Two tenant accounts with overlapping data exist
cases.note: Round 1: the job scope had no tenant, so the tenant-scoped query returned an empty set without raising an error. Fixed and retested in round 2.

cases.description: Messages queued during a consumer outage are processed after restart
cases.procedure:
1. Stop the RabbitMQ consumer service.
2. Send three inbound messages from the channel.
3. Start the consumer again.
cases.expected: All three messages are ingested in order after the consumer restarts; none is lost.
cases.precondition: RabbitMQ queue durability is enabled

cases.description: A duplicate message delivered by a second consumer instance is not processed twice
cases.procedure:
1. Start a second consumer instance.
2. Deliver one inbound message to the queue.
cases.expected: Only one consumer processes the message; no duplicate reply is sent.
cases.precondition: RabbitMQ is configured with exclusive consumer or logical dedup

cases.description: A KB deploy failure leaves the previously deployed version active
cases.procedure:
1. Deploy a version while Qdrant is unavailable.
2. Check which version is active after the deploy job fails.
cases.expected: The deploy job fails and is logged; the previous deployed version remains active for retrieval.
cases.precondition: A deployed version exists; Qdrant can be temporarily stopped

cases.description: KB deploy retries succeed once the vector store recovers
cases.procedure:
1. Restore Qdrant after it was stopped in TC-ST-REC-006.
2. Re-trigger the deploy job.
cases.expected: The deploy job completes successfully; the new version becomes active.
cases.precondition: TC-ST-REC-006 completed; Qdrant is restored

cases.description: Retry of a failed KB deploy leaves prior version active until success
cases.procedure:
1. Fail a deploy with Qdrant down.
2. Restore Qdrant and redeploy.
cases.expected: First deploy fails and is logged; second deploy succeeds and activates the new version.
cases.precondition: Previous deployed version exists

cases.description: Error log entry survives service restart
cases.procedure:
1. Record a job failure.
2. Restart the API service.
3. GET /api/logs/errors.
cases.expected: Error entry is still present after restart.
cases.precondition: Error log is persisted to the database

workflows.name: WF04 Lead Pipeline
workflows.objective: Verify the full lead lifecycle: contact creation, automatic scoring and stage advancement, manual override, handoff to won or lost, and reactivation on renewed inbound contact
workflows.precondition: The full stack is running (all services up); an admin seed account exists; lead scoring rules are seeded via POST /api/lead-scoring-rules/seed-defaults

cases.description: A new conversation from Facebook creates a lead in cold stage
cases.procedure:
1. Simulate an inbound Facebook message.
2. Allow the auto-reply and lead-creation agent to run.
3. GET /api/leads and filter by contactId.
cases.expected: A lead is created with stage=cold and score=0; the contact is linked.
cases.precondition: No existing lead for the contact

cases.description: Score advances the lead from cold to warm after price inquiry activities
cases.procedure:
1. Record asked_price and fast_reply activities via POST /api/leads/{id}/activities.
2. GET /api/leads/{id}.
cases.expected: score >= 30; stage=warm.
cases.precondition: Lead is in cold stage; scoring rules are seeded

cases.description: Enough purchase-intent signals advance the lead to hot
cases.procedure:
1. Record purchase_intent activities until score >= 70.
2. GET /api/leads/{id}.
cases.expected: stage=hot; score >= 70.
cases.precondition: Lead is in warm stage

cases.description: A sales agent manually moves a hot lead to won
cases.procedure: 1. POST /api/leads/{id}/stage with stage=won.
cases.expected: HTTP 200; stage=won; WonAt timestamp is set; the lead no longer appears in active pipeline views.
cases.precondition: Lead is in hot stage

cases.description: A hot lead is moved to lost and a reason is recorded
cases.procedure: 1. POST /api/leads/{id}/stage with stage=lost and reason.
cases.expected: HTTP 200; stage=lost; LostReason is stored.
cases.precondition: Lead is in hot stage

cases.description: A lost lead is reactivated when the customer sends a new message
cases.procedure:
1. Simulate an inbound message from the lost lead contact.
2. GET /api/leads/{id}.
cases.expected: Lead status returns to active; LastActivityAt is updated; stage resets to warm (not cold).
cases.precondition: A lost lead exists; the contact has an active conversation channel

cases.description: Forecast shows the correct count and estimated value for hot leads
cases.procedure: 1. GET /api/leads/forecast.
cases.expected: Response includes hot lead count and summed estimated value; numbers match the current database state.
cases.precondition: At least two leads are in hot stage

cases.description: Re-scoring all leads after a rule change updates stages in bulk
cases.procedure:
1. Update the purchase_intent delta via PUT /api/lead-scoring-rules/{id}.
2. POST /api/leads/rescore-all.
cases.expected: All affected leads have their scores and stages recalculated; no leads are left with a stale score.
cases.precondition: Multiple leads with purchase_intent activities exist
cases.note: Round 1: one broken record aborted the batch and the remaining leads kept their old stage. Fixed and retested in round 2.

cases.description: Lead search by contact name
cases.procedure: 1. GET /api/leads?search={contactName}.
cases.expected: Only leads whose contact name matches are returned.
cases.precondition: Multiple contacts with distinct names exist

cases.description: Stage history is recorded for audit
cases.procedure:
1. Move a lead through cold to warm to hot.
2. GET /api/leads/{id} and inspect stage history.
cases.expected: History entries contain each stage, actor and timestamp.
cases.precondition: Lead is cold

workflows.name: WF05 Content Pipeline
workflows.objective: Verify the end-to-end content pipeline: brief creation, AI generation with lint, agent review, human approval, scheduling at the golden hour and simulated publish
workflows.precondition: The full stack is running (all services up); a configured LLM provider is active; a deployed KB module exists for RAG context

cases.description: A content brief triggers AI generation and produces a draft item
cases.procedure:
1. POST /api/content/briefs with platform=facebook and topic.
2. POST /api/content/items/generate with the briefId.
3. Poll until item status=draft.
cases.expected: A content item with a non-empty body is created in draft status within 60 seconds.
cases.precondition: LLM provider responds within the configured timeout
cases.note: Round 1: the draft was produced but the dialog crashed because the job summary was serialised with the wrong casing. Fixed and retested in round 2.

cases.description: Lint blocks a draft that contains an absolute guarantee phrase
cases.procedure:
1. Generate a draft using a stub that returns a body containing the phrase "100% guaranteed".
2. Check item status.
cases.expected: Item status=needs_human; lint error code is reported.
cases.precondition: LLM stub is configured; ContentLint is enabled

cases.description: Agent reviewer approves a clean draft and it becomes ready for human approval
cases.procedure:
1. Wait for the reviewer agent run to complete on the draft item.
2. GET /api/content/items/{id}.
cases.expected: AgentReviewStatus=passed; item is in the human approval queue.
cases.precondition: Reviewer agent is bound to an LLM provider; draft item is clean

cases.description: A human approves the item and it becomes approved
cases.procedure: 1. POST /api/content/items/{id}/approve.
cases.expected: HTTP 200; status=approved; ApprovedAt and ApprovedBy are recorded.
cases.precondition: Item has passed agent review

cases.description: A human rejects a draft and provides a reason
cases.procedure: 1. POST /api/content/items/{id}/reject with reason="off-brand tone".
cases.expected: HTTP 200; status=rejected; RejectedReason=off-brand tone.
cases.precondition: Item is in draft or needs_human state

cases.description: An approved item is scheduled for the Facebook golden hour
cases.procedure:
1. Calculate the next Facebook golden hour (20:30 VN time).
2. POST /api/content/items/{id}/schedule with publishAt set to that time.
cases.expected: HTTP 200; status=scheduled; publishAt matches the golden hour.
cases.precondition: Item is approved

cases.description: A published item is repurposed for TikTok
cases.procedure: 1. POST /api/content/items/{id}/repurpose with targetPlatform=tiktok.
cases.expected: HTTP 202; a new draft item is created for tiktok; the original item status is unchanged.
cases.precondition: A published item exists; a brief for tiktok exists

cases.description: Chain metrics are recorded after a successful publish
cases.procedure:
1. Trigger a simulated publish for the scheduled item.
2. GET /api/content/chain-metrics.
cases.expected: A metric entry exists for the chain run; generation and review latencies are recorded.
cases.precondition: The mock publish adapter is active

cases.description: Content item audit shows who approved it
cases.procedure:
1. Approve an item as user U.
2. GET /api/content/items/{id}.
cases.expected: ApprovedBy equals U; ApprovedAt is within 60 seconds.
cases.precondition: Item is eligible for approval

cases.description: Expired scheduled item is not published automatically without publish job
cases.procedure:
1. Schedule an item in the past.
2. Do not run the publish job.
cases.expected: Item stays scheduled; no publish occurs.
cases.precondition: Item is approved

workflows.name: WF06 Document & Reporting
workflows.objective: Verify the full path from a live conversation to a personalized quote PDF, its delivery, and its appearance in the KPI report
workflows.precondition: The full stack is running; a conversation with an identified contact and a discussed package exists

cases.description: Sale generates a quote PDF from an active conversation
cases.procedure:
1. Sign in as a sale user.
2. Open the conversation and click Generate Quote.
3. Wait for the document to become ready.
cases.expected: A PDF is produced with the contact's name and the discussed package within 30 seconds.
cases.precondition: The conversation has a contact and a proposed package

cases.description: The generated quote is sent through the same channel
cases.procedure:
1. Click Send on the ready document.
2. Check the conversation timeline.
cases.expected: A message with the document link appears as an outbound message on the same channel.
cases.precondition: TC-ST-DOC-001 completed

cases.description: The document appears in the customer's document library
cases.procedure: 1. Open /documents and filter by the contact.
cases.expected: The generated quote is listed with its sent timestamp and channel.
cases.precondition: TC-ST-DOC-002 completed

cases.description: The document generation event appears in the daily KPI report
cases.procedure: 1. Open /reports for the day the document was generated.
cases.expected: The documents-generated counter includes the new document.
cases.precondition: TC-ST-DOC-001 completed on the report day

cases.description: A scheduled weekly report is delivered to the configured recipient
cases.procedure:
1. Configure a weekly report schedule.
2. Advance to the scheduled time.
3. Check the recipient's notification list.
cases.expected: A report notification or email is delivered at the scheduled time with the correct date range.
cases.precondition: A report schedule is configured
cases.note: Round 1: the scheduler used the server's local time instead of the tenant's configured timezone, so delivery was three hours late. Fixed and retested in round 2.

cases.description: Report export CSV total matches the dashboard total
cases.procedure:
1. Export the same date range as CSV.
2. Sum the export rows and compare to the dashboard total.
cases.expected: The two totals match exactly.
cases.precondition: kpi_daily rows exist for the range

cases.description: Expired document link is not reachable from the report drill-down
cases.procedure:
1. Open the report entry for a document generated more than 7 days ago.
2. Click through to the document link.
cases.expected: The link shows an expired state instead of streaming the file.
cases.precondition: A document older than the expiry window exists

workflows.name: WF07 Admin & Access Control
workflows.objective: Verify end-to-end RBAC: an admin provisions a role and a user, issues an API key, and every fence holds at the system level
workflows.precondition: The full stack is running; an admin seed account exists

cases.description: Admin creates a custom role and assigns it to a new user
cases.procedure:
1. Sign in as tenant admin.
2. Create a role with only conversations:read.
3. Create a user with that role.
cases.expected: The new user is created; the role is attached.
cases.precondition: Permission catalog includes conversations:read

cases.description: The new user's navigation reflects the restricted role
cases.procedure: 1. Sign in as the new user.
cases.expected: Only the Inbox section is visible; other sections are absent from the navigation.
cases.precondition: TC-ST-RBA-001 completed

cases.description: The restricted user cannot call a write endpoint outside their role
cases.procedure: 1. As the new user, POST /api/leads.
cases.expected: HTTP 403; no lead row is created.
cases.precondition: TC-ST-RBA-001 completed

cases.description: Admin issues a read-only API key for an integration
cases.procedure:
1. Create an API key with scope=read.
2. Call a read endpoint then a write endpoint with the key.
cases.expected: The read call succeeds; the write call is rejected with HTTP 403.
cases.precondition: Admin holds api-keys:write

cases.description: Revoking the API key takes effect on the very next call
cases.procedure:
1. Revoke the key from TC-ST-RBA-004.
2. Immediately retry the read call.
cases.expected: HTTP 401 on the next call; no grace period is observed.
cases.precondition: TC-ST-RBA-004 completed

cases.description: Every provisioning action is visible in the audit trail
cases.procedure: 1. Open /admin/audit and filter by today.
cases.expected: Role creation, user creation, key issuance and key revocation each appear with actor and timestamp.
cases.precondition: TC-ST-RBA-001 through 005 completed today
cases.note: Round 1: the API key revoke action was not wired to the audit writer, so it was silently missing from the trail. Fixed and retested in round 2.

cases.description: Deactivating the provisioned user revokes access immediately
cases.procedure:
1. Deactivate the user created in TC-ST-RBA-001.
2. Retry any authenticated call with that user's still-open session.
cases.expected: The next request is rejected with HTTP 403; the session cannot be used further.
cases.precondition: The user has an open session
